Single-cell: embeddings

Source: vignettes/articles/sc-embeddings.Rmd
sc-embeddings.Rmd

Question: where do groups of cells sit on the embedding, and where is a gene or score high?

Function Use
DimPlot_bioToolkit() cells coloured by a group (cell type, cluster, condition)
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit() cells coloured by a value (gene, QC metric, module score)
transform_embedding() flip or rotate an embedding to a conventional orientation
format_sc_plots(), manipulate_sc_plot(), add_dimension_arrows() restyle plots made by Seurat, scCustomize, SCpubr …

Both plot functions keep Seurat’s arguments (group.by, split.by, features, reduction, cells, cols, pt.size, label) and draw panels of a fixed size, with dimension arrows in place of axes.

Data: 8,000 PBMCs from Kang et al. 2018, 8 donors, control or interferon-β (IFN-β) for 6 h; log-normalized, Harmony integration over condition, UMAP; the authors’ cell type labels.

pbmc <- docs_kang()
pbmc
#> An object of class Seurat 
#> 11428 features across 8000 samples within 1 assay 
#> Active assay: RNA (11428 features, 2000 variable features)
#>  2 layers present: counts, data
#>  4 dimensional reductions calculated: pca, umap.unintegrated, harmony, umap
head(pbmc[[]], 3)
#>                  orig.ident nCount_RNA nFeature_RNA donor condition
#> AAACATACCATGCA-1   Kang2018        703          337 D1488   Control
#> AAACATACGCCAAT-1   Kang2018       1140          434 D1016   Control
#> AAACATACGCTTCC-1   Kang2018        817          427 D1256   Control
#>                         sample cell_type
#> AAACATACCATGCA-1 D1488_Control     CD4 T
#> AAACATACGCCAAT-1 D1016_Control CD14 Mono
#> AAACATACGCTTCC-1 D1256_Control     CD4 T

Cells by group 

DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", label = TRUE)

Variants

One panel per level of a second variable; all panels share one legend and one size.

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 3
)

Colour some cells and draw the rest in grey, e.g. one cell type:

mono <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$cell_type %in% c("CD14 Mono", "FCGR3A Mono")]
DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", cells.highlight = mono)

Plot a subset only. full.extent = TRUE keeps the axes of the whole object, so that the subset lines up with the full plot:

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    cells = mono,
    full.extent = TRUE
)

An outline around the cell clouds; outline.color = "darken" uses a darker shade of each group’s colour.

DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", outline = TRUE)

Colour by a fine annotation and outline a broader one (mark.by) with a dashed line around each cloud. Cells with no mark.by group (here the few, scattered megakaryocytes) are not outlined:

lineage <- c(
    "CD4 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD8 T" = "Lymphoid",
    "NK" = "Lymphoid",
    "B" = "Lymphoid",
    "CD14 Mono" = "Myeloid",
    "FCGR3A Mono" = "Myeloid",
    "DC" = "Myeloid",
    "Megakaryocyte" = NA
)
pbmc$lineage <- factor(
    unname(lineage[as.character(pbmc$cell_type)]),
    levels = c("Lymphoid", "Myeloid")
)
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    mark = TRUE,
    mark.by = "lineage",
    mark.cols = c("grey30", "#B5338A")
)

legend.position takes “right”, “left”, “top”, “bottom”, “inside” (in the empty corner of the panel) or “none”.

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "condition",
    legend.position = "inside",
    cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)

Integration and the embedding

The default reduction is “umap”. This object also holds the UMAP computed before integration: stimulated and control cells were captured separately and IFN-β changes the expression of every cell type, so without integration the two conditions form separate clouds. Any reduction of the object can be plotted:

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "condition",
    reduction = "umap.unintegrated",
    cols = c("grey60", "#B5338A")
)

Where the arrows go

With several panels, the dimension arrows are drawn once, in the bottom left panel, by default. arrow.panels puts them in every panel, or in the panels along one edge of the grid: "left" / "right" (the first / last panel of each row) and "top" / "bottom" (the top / lowest panel of each column). In a grid whose last row is incomplete, a panel with nothing below it is on the bottom edge. The same argument works in FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(), DensityDiffPlot_bioToolkit() and format_sc_plots().

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none"
)

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.panels = "left"
)

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.panels = "bottom"
)

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "donor",
    ncol = 3,
    panel.width = 1.6,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.panels = "all"
)

Arrow size

The arrows keep the same proportion to the panel at any size: 2 cm long on a 3.5-inch panel, and scaled with the panel’s shorter side, labels included. Small panels get small arrows that stay clear of the cells near the edges, large panels larger ones. arrow.scale makes them larger or smaller at any panel size (default 1); it works in every function that draws the arrows.

DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 2,
    legend.position = "none",
    arrow.scale = 1.3
)

Genes and scores 

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = c("CD3E", "MS4A1", "CD14", "FCGR3A"),
    ncol = 2,
    panel.width = 2.5
)

Cells with no expression (0) are drawn in grey, apart from the colour scale, so that “not detected” is not confused with “low” (na.cutoff = "auto"). Gene names are set in italics.

Variants

One gene across conditions, on one shared scale (keep.scale = "feature"): ISG15, an interferon-stimulated gene, is induced in every cell type.

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "ISG15",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 3
)

Scores centred on 0 get a diverging scale automatically (diverging = "auto"): the centre colour stays at 0 and each side reaches its full colour at its own extreme, so a score from -0.2 to 1.5 is not faded on the negative side. Here, Seurat’s AddModuleScore() on the MSigDB Hallmark interferon-α response genes (IFN-α and IFN-β signal through the same receptor and induce the same genes):

hallmark <- msigdbr::msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", collection = "H")
is_ifn <- hallmark$gs_name == "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE"
ifn_genes <- intersect(hallmark$gene_symbol[is_ifn], rownames(pbmc))
pbmc <- Seurat::AddModuleScore(
    pbmc,
    features = list(ifn_genes),
    name = "IFN_alpha_score",
    seed = 1
)
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "IFN_alpha_score1",
    split.by = "condition",
    panel.width = 3,
    legend.title = "IFN-α\nresponse"
)

Any metadata column, e.g. a QC metric; max.cutoff caps the scale at a quantile so that a few extreme cells do not compress it:

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "nCount_RNA",
    max.cutoff = "q99",
    cols = "viridis"
)

Label groups (active identities, or label.by) on top of the values:

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CD14",
    label = TRUE,
    label.by = "cell_type"
)

Sparse genes: geom

Most cells have zero counts for many genes, even where the gene is expressed (dropout). Three ways to draw them, here for the chemokine CXCL10, induced by interferon in monocytes:

Every cell coloured by its own value (default).

cxcl10 <- colnames(pbmc)[pbmc$condition == "IFN-beta"]
FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    cells = cxcl10,
    panel.width = 3
)

Cells binned into hexagons. hex.fun = "mean" colours by the mean value in a tile (zeros included); hex.fun = "pct" by the % of cells expressing it.

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    cells = cxcl10,
    geom = "hex",
    hex.fun = "pct",
    panel.width = 3
)

Values smoothed over neighbouring cells. density.method = "smooth" (a kernel-weighted mean, in the units of the feature); "wkde" is the weighted kernel density of the Nebulosa package, scaled to a maximum of 1.

FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc,
    features = "CXCL10",
    cells = cxcl10,
    geom = "density",
    panel.width = 3
)

Orienting an embedding

UMAP coordinates have no meaningful direction. transform_embedding() flips and / or rotates (rotate, in degrees) a 2-D reduction in the object, for display only (distances are unchanged), e.g. to keep the orientation of a published figure:

pbmc_t <- transform_embedding(pbmc, reduction = "umap", flip_vertical = TRUE)
DimPlot_bioToolkit(
    pbmc_t,
    group.by = "cell_type",
    label = TRUE,
    panel.width = 3
)

Restyling plots made by Seurat

format_sc_plots() applies the same look to plots made by other packages: axes replaced by dimension arrows (by default on the bottom left plot only; arrow.panels as above), legends removed or moved, and the plots arranged in a grid. It also takes plots made separately with DimPlot_bioToolkit() or FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(): the arrows they have are replaced, so that each plot keeps at most one set.

seurat_plots <- list(
    Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", reduction = "umap"),
    Seurat::FeaturePlot(pbmc, features = "ISG15", reduction = "umap")
)
format_sc_plots(seurat_plots, ncol = 2)

own_plots <- list(
    DimPlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, group.by = "cell_type", panel.width = 2.2),
    FeaturePlot_bioToolkit(pbmc, features = "ISG15", panel.width = 2.2)
)
format_sc_plots(own_plots, ncol = 2, arrow.panels = "all")

For a single plot, add_dimension_arrows() adds the arrows and manipulate_sc_plot() changes its axes, legend or grid:

p <- Seurat::DimPlot(pbmc, group.by = "condition", reduction = "umap")
p <- manipulate_sc_plot(p, remove.grid = TRUE, legend.title = "Condition")
add_dimension_arrows(p, reduction = "umap", arrow.scale = 0.8)

Plots made by Seurat have no fixed panel size, so give save_plot() a width and height in inches; the arrows are scaled with the panel size they are drawn at. Arguments of these three functions were renamed to dot.case in 0.10.0; add.arrow and bottom.left.only of format_sc_plots() were replaced by arrow.panels in 1.0.0. The old names still work, with a deprecation warning.
